q1: SELECT DISTINCT Y.A AS A FROM R AS X, R AS Y WHERE X.A = Y.A
q2: SELECT DISTINCT X.A AS A FROM R AS X
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT Y.A AS A FROM R AS X, R AS Y WHERE X.A = Y.A
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT X.A AS A FROM R AS X
explanation: Both Q1 and Q2 return distinct values of column A from table R. Q1 uses a self-join on R where X.A = Y.A, which effectively produces all values of A from R, and DISTINCT ensures no duplicates. Q2 directly selects distinct A from R. Since the join condition X.A = Y.A is always true for any row in R when joining R with itself on A, Q1 and Q2 are semantically equivalent.
